Mĕtăpīnus , a, um etym. dub.,
I.Metapinic, an epithet of the second or middle of the three principal mouths of the Rhone: “cujus ora appellata ... alterum Metapinum,” Mart. Cap. 6, § 635 ; Plin. 3, 4, 5, § 32.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
